system.name: Melange validation protocol and prospective tests
system.description: How claims in the Melange models are tested. Covers single-look holdout discipline, gold-set validation, the zero-rank-delta gate, the frozen forecast ledger, the prospective receptivity outcome contract (H1/H2), the receptivity sensitivity harness, Monte Carlo stability and method audits, and the F5 power gate.

components.name: Single-look holdout discipline and look ledger
components.computes: Pass or miss of pre-registered confirmatory looks.
components.method: The gate is pre-registered with hashes; a look is consumed once and never re-run; look fragments are void. A joint-null simulation gives about 1.5-2% false pass.
empirical_questions: What is the empirical false-discovery rate of this protocol across the look ledger?
components.heading: Single-look holdout discipline and look ledger

components.name: Gold-set validation and zero-rank-delta gate
components.computes: Trust scores against owner-ruled gold sets, and a byte-identical ranks_python.json check for behaviour-preserving changes.
components.method: Gold sets: 400 tweets, 760 press rows, Senate panels. Freshness: warn after 7 days, fail after 14.
assumptions: Gold labels are independent of the pipeline
empirical_questions: How much do gold-set accuracies differ from accuracy on randomly sampled live rows?
components.heading: Gold-set validation and zero-rank-delta gate

components.name: Prospective receptivity contract (H1/H2) and forecast ledger
components.computes: H1: Spearman(seed_prob, new cosponsorship). H2: Spearman(pressure_mult, |tier movement|). Frozen cosponsor-join and dyad-persistence (p = 0.82) forecasts with Brier scores.
components.method: Bars: >= .20 PASS, .10-.20 DIRECTIONAL, <= -.10 INDICTED. Needs at least 60 days and 150 movers. One look per contract.
assumptions: Cross-sectional Spearman is a valid test
empirical_questions: Does seed_prob predict which members add CU cosponsorships after the freeze date?
components.heading: Prospective receptivity contract (H1-H2) and forecast ledger

components.name: Receptivity sensitivity harness, MC stability and F5 power gate
components.computes: Top-20/50 target overlap under constant sweeps; seed-set stability across MC budgets; H1/H2 power (requires at least 150 new-event members).
components.method: ROBUST at top-20 overlap >= 18. The F5 replay found 72 of 511 new-event members (UNDERPOWERED; look unspent).
assumptions: A robust target set means the constant cannot change a decision
empirical_questions: Which receptivity constants change targeting decisions, and are those the ones with weakest literature support?
components.heading: Receptivity sensitivity harness, MC stability and F5 power gate

evidence.title: A causal approach for detecting team-level momentum in NBA games
evidence.claim: The authors argue that comparing points before and after a coach-called timeout is fallacious because coaches often call timeouts to stop momentum. They use TV timeouts, which fall at predetermined times, and match runs interrupted by a TV timeout to uninterrupted runs on propensity scores (pairs; unmatched runs dropped). Result: -11.2% points over the next 3 minutes (b = -0.119, SE 0.012), n = 5,148 matched runs. Caveat from the same paper: Appendix E (as described in the main text) finds coaches' timeouts give largely similar, slightly larger effects, and the TV-vs-coach coefficient difference was not significant; Sec. 5.3 concedes TV timeouts may not be fully exogenous.
evidence.system_side: H2 scores frozen pressure_mult against |overall-tier movement| with an unadjusted cross-sectional Spearman. PROTOCOL_TEXT plans an engaged-only run among members the In-contact log marks engaged, but states it is unavailable until separately specified, receipted contact data exists; the result field is engaged_only = NOT_IMPLEMENTED_NO_CONTACT_CONTRACT. CLAIM_SCOPE = receptivity_forecast_only_not_spending_effects.
evidence.transfer: Design logic only, not effect size. Lobbyist-chosen contact is endogenous like a coach's timeout, so an engaged-only rho would confound pressure_mult with targeting unless contact timing is exogenous or matched on targeting covariates. The engaged-only arm is a subgroup correlation, not a before/after-contact comparison, so the analogy is to the selection problem, not an identical design. The paper's own Appendix E finding (coach vs TV timeouts not significantly different) means it does not empirically show the endogenous design is badly biased in its setting. Single observational study with matching.

evidence.title: A causal approach for detecting team-level momentum in NBA games
evidence.claim: A Monte Carlo with zero true momentum (130,000 independent 50/50 scoring plays, a TV timeout after one play in every 50, substitutions not simulated) yields a null treatment coefficient (b = 0.002, SE 0.022, n = 1,336). The Fig. 6 caption calls it a negative control showing the matched design does not find an effect where none exists.
evidence.system_side: The discipline already used a simulated null to calibrate its protocol: a joint-null false-pass simulation (pass-both-panels about 1.5-2%, dual dominance under 1%) supported exactly one more look per trait.
evidence.transfer: Supports the general practice of simulating under a known null to check that a selection or gating rule cannot manufacture a pass. Says nothing about the 1.5-2% figure or pre-registration; the brain simulation concerns look false-pass rates, not engine outcome estimators.

evidence.title: A causal approach for detecting team-level momentum in NBA games
evidence.claim: Appendix D (described in the main text) re-tallies post-treatment points over windows from 60 s to 4 minutes in 10 s steps; the negative effect persists but the point estimate steadily decreases as the window lengthens, and there is no significant effect for points scored between minutes 3 and 4. The first-minute effect is about four times the 3-minute effect.
evidence.system_side: mc_stability_check.py reruns one topic's budget frontier at MC=20/100 and SEED=7/1/13 and reports Jaccard set overlap; receptivity_sensitivity.py sweeps receptivity constants and labels ROBUST when top-20 overlap >= 18. The outcome contract has no window sweep: the window is whatever elapses between freeze and score, with a 60-day minimum and 150 movers before it stops returning UNDERPOWERED.
evidence.transfer: Suggests pre-registering a small set of outcome windows inside the contract lock rather than choosing one afterward (basis-shopping). Minute-scale decay says nothing about congressional time scales.

evidence.title: Introduction To Monte Carlo Simulation
evidence.claim: The paper reports no error analysis, convergence diagnostic or comparison of samplers. On randomness quality it says LCGs do not do well on many Diehard-type tests and that the Mersenne Twister is becoming the generator of choice, passing most tests except some for encryption RNGs.
evidence.system_side: mc_stability_check.py reruns the single-topic frontier at MC = 100 (SEED 7) and at MC = 20 with SEED 1 and 13, comparing picked seed sets by Jaccard overlap, first-k identical picks and final-spread delta. It sets no numeric pass bar. Bystander rolls in scenario.py use Python random (Mersenne Twister). Edge draws use splitmix64, which the paper does not discuss.
evidence.transfer: The system goes further than the source. The paper can endorse the generator choice but supplies no criterion for MC budget or stability. The ROBUST bar (top-20 overlap >= 18) lives in fec/members/receptivity_sensitivity.py:113, a constant-sensitivity check, not in mc_stability_check.py; any MC-stability bar would have to come from elsewhere (the script's docstring cites Almazaydeh et al. 2026 as motivation only).

evidence.title: Do Politicians Take Risks Like the Rest of Us? An Experimental Test of Prospect Theory Under MPs
evidence.claim: Outside the Asian disease problem, the political-scenario reflection effect is weak: only the votes+economic scenario shows it (85% vs 69.23%, Fisher p=0.302; significant only as a scenario interaction in the pooled regression, OR 8.684, p=0.033), and the paper reports no loss aversion. Effect direction for an electoral pt domain is therefore uncertain, and the size of LOSSFRAME is unsupported.
evidence.system_side: The receptivity sensitivity sweep varies PT only from 1.15/0.92 to 1.10/0.95 (mild) and to 1.25/0.85 (strong). It has no PT-off (1.0/1.0) or reversed variant and does not sweep LOSSFRAME.
evidence.transfer: Applies directly. Adding a pt = 1.0/1.0 arm and a LOSSFRAME = 1.0 arm to the existing top-20/50 overlap harness would show whether either constant changes targeting decisions. Diagnostic sweep, not a confirmatory look.

evidence.title: How Do Electoral Incentives Affect Legislator Behavior? Evidence from U.S. State Legislatures
evidence.claim: In the final term, effort falls (sponsorship -6%, committee activity -8%, participation -2.7 points) while positions stay flat (W-NOMINATE and interest-group nulls).
evidence.system_side: Under the protocol, H2 (labelled Byrne/F&H) tests Spearman(frozen pressure_mult, |overall-tier movement|) after the freeze. pressure_mult carries the 0.60 retiring factor. Tier movement depends on new evidence events, and retiring members produce fewer of them under this paper's effect, so a positive H2 could arise mechanically from lower activity rather than from responsiveness. The paper also predicts no true position change from the F&H channel.
evidence.transfer: Moderate as a threat to interpretation. It applies only if tier movement is driven by evidence volume. If the contract is still unfrozen, a reported retiring/other-office stratum could be added. If it is frozen, any H2 result should carry this caveat. This is analysis, not a look, and stays UNVERIFIED until reproduced (DE-062).

evidence.title: The Effect of Political Advertising after Citizens United: Adjusting for Unmeasured Confounding in Marginal Structural Models
evidence.claim: Placebo tests check the identifying assumptions by applying the estimator to outcomes measured before treatment: the previous election's vote share and turnout, and the pre-election poll share. IPTW-FE estimates are near zero, while the naive approach shows residual confounding for some Democratic-ad effects.
evidence.system_side: H1 is a Spearman correlation between the frozen seed_prob and new cosponsorships after the freeze. H2 is a Spearman correlation between pressure_mult and absolute tier movement. Both are cross-sectional, with no pre-freeze placebo. The contract requires at least 60 days and 150 movers, and returns UNDERPOWERED without consuming the look.
evidence.transfer: The placebo logic carries over directly. A pre-registered negative control would be Spearman(seed_prob, cosponsorship delta over a window that ends before the freeze). A non-zero value would show that seed_prob tracks a stable member trait (a time-constant confounder) rather than responsiveness. Adding it changes the contract, so it needs Paul's ruling before the single look is spent, and it needs a second pre-freeze snapshot pair. Neither H1 nor H2 measures a lobbying treatment, so even a PASS remains an association.

evidence.title: Measuring Interest Group Positions on Legislation: An AI-Driven Analysis of Lobbying Reports
evidence.claim: LLM labels agree with human coders at 96.93% accuracy and F1 97.19, but only on the 391 samples where two coders agreed. MapLight concordance is 91.03% (1,076 of 1,182 pairs) and covers Support/Oppose only; MapLight labels were also part of the GNN training labels. GNN best configuration: accuracy 78.51, F1 74.65; per-class F1 Support 79.19, Oppose 64.06, Engage 80.70.
evidence.system_side: The system's benchmark of the Kim-format Haiku lane uses the 876 (organisation, bill) pairs where Kim's published dataset overlaps the system's work items, at natural base rates with no stratification, and separates Kim's two annotation lanes (541 gnn pairs, 335 llm pairs). The join module records Support/Oppose recall 0.49 and precision 0.42, and Amend 0 found against Kim's 23. The DEBATE 0.571 adversarial-frame figure comes from audit documents, not these files.
evidence.transfer: The paper's human validation uses only coder-agreed lines, so its 96.93% does not carry over to ambiguous, Amend or Mention lines. The system benchmark measures agreement with Kim's labels, not accuracy: 541 of its 876 reference pairs are Kim GNN predictions (a stage with 78.51% test accuracy) and 335 are GPT-4 labels. Denominator: the 876-pair overlap (the benchmark file states no year window). UNVERIFIED as accuracy until a human-gold path reproduces it (DE-062).

evidence.title: Mathematical Modeling, Analysis and Simulation Utilizing Machine Learning Tools for Assessing the Impact of Climate Lobbying
evidence.claim: Varying the centrist-flow parameters by 10% produces a wide spread of final C, Y and N counts. In the parameter-impact ranking, centrist-lobbying parameters (M_LF, M_LA) and tau rank high and initial compartment sizes rank low. Linear SVMs on 1000-sample sweeps find no clean pass/fail boundary in multi-parameter sweeps.
evidence.system_side: The receptivity sensitivity harness sweeps only receptivity constants: susc scale, prospect-theory multipliers, retiring factor and persona weight (VARIANTS). It grades each by top-20 overlap (ROBUST at 18 or more). The harness does not sweep the flip model's channel weights WM/WP (0.35/0.65) or the PERS persuadability table. The one centrist-like knob that has been swept, PERS_NONE, was swept by hand and recorded in a comment: top-20 overlap was 16/18/20/18/15 across 0.30-0.95, and total winnability ran from 149.5 to 245.8.
evidence.transfer: The transfer is a method idea, not evidence. Jacoby's sensitivity comes from a well-mixed ODE model with literature-fixed parameters, and the system's flip model is a network-based ratio of saturating terms. What carries over is the diagnostic: the parameters that decide who is movable and how fast they move should be swept first. The pass/fail SVM is not needed, because top-k overlap already measures decision change. Any such sweep is a bound on the model, not validation (DE-062).

evidence.title: Campaign Contributions Facilitate Access to Congressional Officials: A Randomized Field Experiment
evidence.claim: The seniority of the official who attends responded to a randomized donor label across 191 offices over about three months. Cosponsorship as an outcome tells us little: nine legislators cosponsored in total, with the same share in both arms, and the authors say the estimate is too uncertain to bear on access effects.
evidence.system_side: H1 correlates frozen seed_prob with new cosponsorship count deltas by Spearman rank, requiring at least 60 days and at least 150 members with any delta. These thresholds match PROTOCOL_TEXT at outcome_contract.py:17-20. The summary's F5 replay figure of 72 of 511 new-event members was not found in the engine code or docs searched.
evidence.transfer: The transfer concerns outcome choice, not effect size. A seniority-of-attendee outcome needs a real outreach log, which the system does not have, plus its own pre-registered single look. Any result stays UNVERIFIED until a second path reproduces it (DE-062). Do not use the 72 of 511 figure until it is located.

evidence.title: Evaluating voice samples as a potential source of information about personality
evidence.claim: No standard test fits the repeated model and feature selection; uncertainty is handled by assuming a generalizable model improves with 100-fold CV (about 9 percent more training data per fold). No permutation null is reported. Post-hoc reliability-performance correlation t(4)=2.65, r=0.80, p=.057, falls to r=0.309 under leave-one-out.
evidence.system_side: The audio prereg used Marrero effect size (r about .25-.33) as the expected signal. A power check found the permutation 95th percentile at +0.267 for N=40 and 88 features, above the locked +0.15 bar. N was raised (fetch eligibility default 80) and a permutation-significance gate applied; audio-E r +0.228 against a permutation floor of +0.234 did not pass.
evidence.transfer: The paper's effect sizes come from N=545 self-report students and have no null distribution, so they should not set a pass bar for an N=90, 88-feature legislator design without a permutation floor. This is consistent with the system's stricter rule.

evidence.title: Optimal Targeting in Fundraising: A Causal Machine-Learning Approach
evidence.claim: Policy gains are identified from randomized assignment through the AIPW score; identifying the causal effect of each covariate is not needed (Section 4.3, Appendix B). The 2014 rule's gains held in a caliper-matched 2015 sample but not in the full 2015 sample (Section 5.6, Table 8). The paper validates with 20-fold cross-validation rather than a single-look holdout (Section 5.3).
evidence.system_side: fec/engine/outcome_contract.py fixes CLAIM_SCOPE to receptivity_forecast_only_not_spending_effects and describes itself as forecasting machinery, never spending-effect evidence. The H1 seeding and H2 pressure tests check rank correlations of frozen features with later cosponsorship and tier movement. No randomized treatment is part of the design.
evidence.transfer: The paper shows the missing design: randomized treatment within strata, which is the precondition for upgrading from forecasting to spending-effect evidence. This is feasible for Terrier contacts or CU outreach logs and not for statutory PAC contributions to legislators. The paper's gains are not evidence for the system.

evidence.title: Contingency-Aware Influence Maximization: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
evidence.claim: q is the probability that a selected node is willing to act as a seed, conditional on being selected or invited. It is assumed known a priori, so it is a take-up rate, not an unconditional outcome.
evidence.system_side: H1 protocol: Spearman correlation of frozen seed_prob with NEW cosponsorships adopted after the freeze, over members with panel coverage in both snapshots. Engaged-only scoring is unavailable until receipted contact data exists. Minimum data is 60 days and 150 members with any delta; otherwise status is UNDERPOWERED (outcome_contract.py:17-21 and 262-263).
evidence.transfer: Unconditional new cosponsorship mixes take-up with contact choice and base activity. A pass would not validate seed_prob as a contingency probability, and a miss would not refute it. The construct match needs an engaged-only arm built on a contact log.

evidence.title: Comparing Fine-Tuned RoBERTa with Traditional Machine Learning Models for Stance Detection in Political Tweets
evidence.claim: Stance is a three-way task in which unrelated is a first-class label alongside agree and disagree. Per-class precision, recall and F1 are reported, with macro averages.
evidence.system_side: stance_eval.py scores any prediction column against adjudicated gold, with macro-F1 as the headline, and its class list includes unrelated. train_tweet_stance.py uses the same four classes and scores with 5-fold stratified CV rather than one split.
evidence.transfer: The labelling and metric conventions transfer across language and domain. The paper gives no cross-validation, no agreement statistic and no confidence interval, so it is a source for the convention only, not for validation rigour.

evidence.title: How to train your stochastic parrot: large language models for political texts
evidence.claim: The recommended validation has three steps: hand-label a small set to design the prompt, validate on a second hand-labelled set (by the team or crowd coders) for strong correlation with ground truth, then apply. Crowd workers increasingly use LLMs (Veselovsky et al. 2023), which threatens crowd-code independence.
evidence.system_side: build_tweet_gold_queue.py writes model_stance and model_margin into the same rows as the human gold_* columns (lines 92-96). The api_* columns are written as blank placeholders reserved for an optional pre-label pass (line 18 and lines 92-96). Low-margin (Q_LOWMARGIN) and anti-bank (Q_ANTIBANK) slices are oversampled (lines 25-27).
evidence.transfer: The paper does not test anchoring on pre-labels, so this is a design implication, not a measured effect. If a labeller sees model_stance, agreement with gold partly measures agreement with the model. Oversampled hard slices make these accuracies incomparable with the paper random-sample 88.4 percent.

evidence.title: An introduction to grf
evidence.claim: Effect heterogeneity is tested by ranking on a score and computing the gain over the ATE in the top-ranked fraction (TOC/AUTOC), which requires treated and untreated units. The authors warn that out-of-bag TOC is a heuristic without finite-sample guarantees and that policy trees need a held-out set (pp.8-11).
evidence.system_side: H1 in the prospective-contract protocol: frozen seed_prob correlates positively with new cosponsorships adopted after the freeze (Spearman over members with panel coverage in both snapshots). This is an association with the outcome level, not a test of whether contact moves high-seed_prob members more.
evidence.transfer: Effect-modification reading applies only if CU outreach or money exposure is logged per member with plausibly known assignment. Otherwise H1 is a predictive-validity check. The held-out, single-look design is consistent with the authors' advice, but this is a judgment, not something the paper tests.

evidence.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction (2nd ed.)
evidence.claim: Before deploying a new policy, Adobe (Theocharous et al.) estimated its value from data logged under other policies, using high-confidence off-policy evaluation with probabilistic improvement guarantees. Logs: about 200,000 interactions from a campaign that randomly offered one of 7 offers, and about 4,000,000 interactions over 12 offers. The test set was real interactions served by a random policy.
evidence.system_side: outcome_contract.py scores frozen predictors by Spearman: seed_prob against new cosponsorship gain (H1), and pressure_mult against the absolute tier movement (H2). Verdict bars: PASS at 0.20 or above, DIRECTIONAL from 0.10 to 0.20, INDICTED at -0.10 or below. Minimum: 60 days and at least 150 members with a positive cosponsorship delta (the movers count in code). The protocol text instead says 150 members with any delta. The contract ranks frozen predictors; it does not estimate the value of a counterfactual policy. The engaged-only contact arm is marked NOT_IMPLEMENTED_NO_CONTACT_CONTRACT.
evidence.transfer: Off-policy estimates for alternative allocations need logged actions with known or estimable propensities and overlap. I did not confirm that funding and contact are logged without propensities beyond the missing contact contract. The claim that real assignment is strategic and near-deterministic is the analyst's assertion and has no support in the code I read. Any such estimate stays UNVERIFIED until a second path reproduces it (DE-062).
